1. # **Introduction** {#introduction}

## **1.1	Purpose** {#1.1-purpose}

This document describes the structure of StartSmart AI, an AI-integrated web application that aims to help university students overcome difficulties in starting academic tasks and manage their study progress. It provides a clear explanation of the system's structure, components, interfaces, and design decisions to guide the development and implementation of the application.

This document is intended for the project development team, including software developers, system designers, testers, and other stakeholders involved in the development, testing, and maintenance of StartSmart AI.

## **1.2	Scope**  {#1.2-scope}

The software product is **StartSmart AI**, an AI-integrated academic task management application for university students who struggle with procrastination, feel overwhelmed by academic tasks, or have difficulty identifying where to begin.

The application aims to help students break down academic tasks into smaller, manageable steps through AI-guided assistance. Its main features include user registration and login, subject and task management, AI-assisted obstacle identification, checklist generation and editing, focus sessions, progress tracking, and exam preparation planning. The application also incorporates a gamification system that rewards students with experience points (XP), achievements, and subject trees to encourage consistent effort.

The scope of this project covers the design and implementation of the core application features within the project development period. Advanced features such as AI vision-board interviews, camera or screen-based AI monitoring, real-time peer collaboration, past-year examination paper analysis, and heatmap calendars are excluded from the current scope and may be considered for future development.

## **1.3	Overview** {#1.3-overview}

The following sections describe the system's personas, system features, sprint planning, and user story details, including activity diagrams and system sequence diagrams to illustrate the interactions between users and the system. The document also covers performance and other requirements, design constraints, a requirements matrix, and test cases to support system verification and validation. 

2. # **Specific Requirements** {#specific-requirements}

## **2.1	Persona** {#2.1-persona}

This section presents the personas representing the target users of the proposed system and their characteristics, needs, and challenges.

### ***2.1.1 Persona 1 (Overwhelmed student)*** {#2.1.1-persona-1-(overwhelmed-student)}

#### **2.1.1.1 Description** {#2.1.1.1-description}

Sarah Lim, 21 years old, a second-year university student who manages several assignments, quizzes, and group projects at the same time. Her motivations and goals are to complete assignments on time, understand what to do first, and make steady academic progress. However, she often delays starting difficult assignments because she does not know where to begin. She tends to overthink the workload and prefers clear, manageable steps. She feels overwhelmed by large tasks, struggles to identify the first step, and finds it difficult to stay motivated when assignments seem complicated. Her technical expertise is that she is comfortable using smartphones, laptops, and common academic applications such as a smart tablet.

#### **2.1.1.2 User Stories** {#2.1.1.2-user-stories}

* US001: As an overwhelmed student, I want the AI to identify what is preventing me from starting a task so that I can receive guidance suited to my difficulty.

* US002: As an overwhelmed student, I want the AI to generate a checklist of small, manageable steps so that I can begin my assignment without feeling overwhelmed.

* US003: As an overwhelmed student, I want to break a difficult step into smaller steps so that I can continue working when I feel stuck.

* US004: As an overwhelmed student, I want to edit my checklist so that I can organize my work according to my needs.

### ***2.1.2 Persona 2 (Easily distracted student)*** {#2.1.2-persona-2-(easily-distracted-student)}

#### **2.1.2.1 Description** {#2.1.2.1-description}

Daniel Tan, 20 years old, a first-year university student who wants to perform well academically but struggles to maintain concentration while studying independently. He wants to finish academic tasks efficiently, develop better study habits, and stay aware of his progress. Unfortunately, he frequently switches between study materials and social media. He sometimes loses track of his progress and finds it difficult to return to a task after becoming distracted. His pain points are difficulty maintaining focus, managing distractions, and staying engaged with long or complicated tasks. He is familiar with web applications, online learning platforms, and digital productivity tools.

#### **2.1.2.2 User Stories** {#2.1.2.2-user-stories}

* US005: As an easily distracted student, I want to start a focus session for a selected task step so that I can concentrate on one clear goal at a time.

* US006: As an easily distracted student, I want to check in on my progress during a focus session so that I can recognize when I am distracted or stuck.

* US007: As an easily distracted student, I want to record what I accomplished after a study session so that I can reflect on my effort.

* US008: As an easily distracted student, I want to view my accumulated experience points and achievements so that I can see my academic progress and stay motivated.


### ***2.1.3 Persona 3 (Exam-preparing student)*** {#2.1.3-persona-3-(exam-preparing-student)}

Ariff Rahman, 22 years old, a third-year university student taking several challenging subjects and preparing for upcoming examinations. His goals are to revise all important topics before examinations, distribute his workload effectively, and monitor his revision progress. He usually understands the importance of revision but sometimes postpones it until the examination date approaches. His pain points are difficult to decide which topics to revise first, allocate time across chapters, and keep track of unfinished revision tasks. He is comfortable using online learning systems, digital calendars, and study applications.

####  **2.1.3.2 User Stories** {#2.1.3.2-user-stories}

* US009: As an exam-preparing student, I want to create a task for an upcoming examination so that I can organize my revision under the relevant subject.

* US010: As an exam-preparing student, I want to generate a revision schedule based on my examination date and topics so that I can plan my revision systematically.

* US011: As an exam-preparing student, I want to view my saved tasks and previous conversations by subject so that I can continue my revision without losing my progress.

* US012: As an exam-preparing student, I want to track completed revision steps so that I can identify which topics still require attention.

## **2.2	System Features** {#2.2-system-features}

The system features are illustrated in Figure 2.2.1 below. The detailed description of each module and functions is tabulated in Table 2.2.2.

**![][image2]**

### ***Figure 2.2.1: Use Case Diagram for StartSmart Web App*** {#figure-2.2.1:-use-case-diagram-for-startsmart-web-app}

***Table 2.2.2: Description of Module and Functions for StartSmart Web App***

| Use Case ID | Function | Description  |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| US001 | Register account | Allows a new student to create an account to save their academic tasks and progress.  |
| US002 | Log in  | Allows a registered student to access their saved subjects, tasks, and progress.  |
| US003 | Manage subjects | Allows a student to create and organize academic subjects.  |
| US004 | Create academic tasks | Allows a student to create a task under a subject and select General or Exam Prep as the task type.  |
| US005 | Identify task obstacles | Allows a student to identify difficulties preventing them from starting a task through AI-guided questions.  |
| US006 | Generate checklist | Allows a student to generate a checklist of manageable steps based on the task details and identified obstacles.  |
| US007 | Edit checklist  | Allows a student to add, delete, reorder, edit, or regenerate checklist steps.  |
| US008 | Update task progress | Allows a student to mark checklist steps as completed or incomplete and view updated progress.  |
| US009 | Request task hint | Allows a student to request a hint for a difficult checklist step.  |
| US010 | View and edit task steps  | Allows a student to divide a difficult step into smaller, more manageable sub-steps.  |
| US011 | Set focus session  | Allows a student to start a timed study session for an unfinished checklist step.  |
| US012 | Perform self check-in  | Allows a student to report whether they are on track, stuck, or distracted during a focus session.  |
| US013 | View session wrap-up | Allows a student to record their accomplishments, update task status, and earn experience points (XP) after a session.  |
| US014 | View progress and achievement  | Allows a student to view accumulated XP, subject trees, and unlocked achievements.  |
| US015 | Generate exam revision schedule  | Allows a student to generate and edit a revision schedule based on an upcoming examination date and selected topics.  |
| US016 | View task history  | Allows a student to access saved conversations, checklists, and previous task progress by subject.  |

## **2.3	Sprint Planning / Launch Phase** {#2.3-sprint-planning-/-launch-phase}

The product backlog holds 16 user stories delivered over 4 sprints, ordered so each sprint ends with something a student can actually use. 

Priority follows MoSCoW: Must \= needed for the core flow, Should \= adds clear value.

| Sprint | Goal | User Stories | Team Members Assigned |
| :---: | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Sprint 1** | A student can sign in, set up subjects and add tasks by hand or from MoodleAI | US001, US002, US003, US004 | To be assigned by the team |
| **Sprint 2** | A student gets an AI-guided checklist for a task, in phases for a big project | US005, US006, US007, US008 | To be assigned by the team |
| **Sprint 3** | A student can work in a Focus Session with a floating bar, get unstuck and earn XP | US010, US011, US012, US013 | To be assigned by the team |
| **Sprint 4** | Hints, progress, exam timetable and history work, system tested | US009, US014, US015, US016 | To be assigned |

## **2.4	User Story Details** {#2.4-user-story-details}

Each story follows the SRS template: description, flow of events, alternative flows, acceptance criteria and exception flows, followed by its sequence diagram and activity diagram. AI-driven steps always have a rule-based fallback, so every story can be tested without depending on what the AI says.

#### **2.4.1 US001: Register Account** {#2.4.1-us001:-register-account}

### ***Table 2.4.1: User Story Description for Register Account*** {#table-2.4.1:-user-story-description-for-register-account}

| User story: Register Account |
| ----- |
| **ID**: US001 |
| **User Story Description** **As a** new student **I want** to create an account **So that** my academic tasks and progress are saved |
| **Flow of events:** 1\.	The student opens the app and selects Register. 2\.	The student enters a name, email and password. 3\.	The system validates the input and creates the account. 4\.	The system logs the student in and shows the home screen with an empty subject list. |
| **Acceptance Criteria** **Precondition:** •	The app is open and the student is not logged in. **Postcondition:** •	An account exists and a logged-in session is active. **Other conditions:** •	The email must be unique and the password must be at least 8 characters. |
| **Exception flow:** E1: Email already registered. The system shows an "email already in use" message and stays on the form. E2: Invalid email format or short password. The system highlights the field and explains the rule. E3: Account creation fails. The system shows an error and keeps the entered data. |

#### **2.4.2 US002: Log In** {#2.4.2-us002:-log-in}

### ***Table 2.4.2: User Story Description for Log In*** {#table-2.4.2:-user-story-description-for-log-in}

| User story: Log In |
| ----- |
| **ID**: US002 |
| **User Story Description** **As a** registered student **I want** to log in **So that** I can see my saved subjects, tasks and progress |
| **Flow of events:** 1\.	The student opens the app and selects Log in. 2\.	The student enters email and password. 3\.	The system verifies them and opens a logged-in session. 4\.	The system shows the home screen with the student's saved subjects. |
| **Alternative flow A1 (log out):** The student selects Log out. The system ends the session and shows the login screen. |
| **Acceptance Criteria** **Precondition:** •	The student has a registered account. **Postcondition:** •	A logged-in session is active and the student's own data is shown. **Other conditions:** •	A student can only see their own subjects, tasks and progress. |
| **Exception flow:** E1: Wrong email or password. The system shows an error and the student stays on the login screen. E2: Empty field. The system highlights it and asks the student to fill it in. |

#### **2.4.3 US003: Manage Subjects** {#2.4.3-us003:-manage-subjects}

### ***Table 2.4.3: User Story Description for Manage Subjects*** {#table-2.4.3:-user-story-description-for-manage-subjects}

| User story: Manage Subjects |
| ----- |
| **ID**: US003 |
| **User Story Description** **As a** student **I want** to create and organise my subjects **So that** my tasks are grouped by course |
| **Flow of events:** 1\.	The student selects Add subject and enters a subject name. 2\.	The system validates the name and saves the subject. 3\.	The system shows the new subject on the home screen. |
| **Alternative flow A1 (rename):** The student selects Edit on a subject, changes the name and saves. The system updates the name everywhere it is shown. |
| **Alternative flow A2 (reorder):** The student drags a subject to a new position. The system saves the order. |
| **Alternative flow A3 (delete):** The student selects Delete. The system shows a confirmation that the subject's tasks, checklists, sessions and fruits will be removed. When the student confirms, the system deletes the subject. If the student cancels, nothing changes. |
| **Acceptance Criteria** **Precondition:** •	The student is logged in. **Postcondition:** •	The subject list is saved in the chosen order. **Other conditions:** •	A subject name cannot be empty and must be unique within the student's list. •	XP already earned is kept after a subject is deleted. |
| **Exception flow:** E1: Empty name. The system shows a validation message and does not save. E2: Duplicate name. The system shows "subject already exists". E3: Saving or deleting fails. The system shows an error and the list stays unchanged. |

#### **2.4.4 US004: Create Academic Tasks** {#2.4.4-us004:-create-academic-tasks}

**Table 2.4.4: User Story Description for Create Academic Tasks**

| User story: Create Academic Tasks |
| ----- |
| **ID**: US004 |
| **User Story Description** **As a** student **I want** to add a task quickly, either by typing it or by importing it from Moodle, and choose General, Exam Prep or Major Project **So that** the app guides me in the right way without extra typing |
| **Flow of events:** 1\.	The student opens a subject and selects Add task. 2\.	The student enters a task description and an optional due date, and chooses a task type: General, Exam Prep or Major Project. Quick add is designed to take about 3 seconds. 3\.	The system saves the task under the subject. 4\.	The system opens the task conversation and starts obstacle identification (US005). |
| **Alternative flow A1 (Exam Prep):** The student chooses Exam Prep. The system requires an exam date and continues in US015. If the exam is in the preloaded timetable (US015), the date is filled in automatically. |
| **Alternative flow A2 (import from Moodle):** The student selects Import from Moodle and pastes their UTM Moodle (eLearning) Calendar URL. The system reads the calendar feed and lists the assignments, labs and deadlines for the student's sections, grouped by subject. The student confirms. The system saves them as General tasks with their due dates, creates any missing subjects and skips tasks that already exist. |
| **Alternative flow A3 (Major Project):** The student chooses Major Project. The task is saved without an exam date, and its checklist is grouped into phases in US006. |
| **Acceptance Criteria** **Precondition:** •	The student is logged in and, for quick add, the subject exists. **Postcondition:** •	The task is stored under its subject with its type. Imported tasks keep the due date given by Moodle. **Other conditions:** •	The task description cannot be empty. An Exam Prep task must have a future exam date. •	The Moodle URL is used only to read the student's own calendar and is treated as private. Quick add stays available at all times. •	Importing the same calendar twice does not create duplicate tasks. |
| **Exception flow:** E1: Empty task description. The system shows a validation message and does not save. E2: Exam date missing or not in the future. The system asks for a valid date. E3: Save fails. The system shows an error and keeps the entered data so the student can retry. E4: The Moodle link is invalid or cannot be reached. The system explains this and the student can add tasks by hand. E5: The calendar has no upcoming items. The system shows "nothing to import". |

#### **2.4.5 US005: Identify Task Obstacles** {#2.4.5-us005:-identify-task-obstacles}

### ***Table 2.4.5: User Story Description for Identify Task Obstacles*** {#table-2.4.5:-user-story-description-for-identify-task-obstacles}

| User story: Identify Task Obstacles |
| ----- |
| **ID**: US005 |
| **User Story Description** **As a** student **I want** the AI to ask a few short questions about what is stopping me **So that** the help I get fits my real difficulty |
| **Flow of events:** 1\.	The system asks up to three short questions about why the task is hard to start, each with selectable options (for example unclear requirements, feeling overwhelmed, not understanding a concept) plus a free-text box. 2\.	The student answers each question. 3\.	The system records the obstacle category with the task and shows a one-line summary of it. 4\.	The student confirms the summary or changes the category. 5\.	The system moves on to checklist generation (US006). |
| **Alternative flow A1 ("not sure"):** The student answers "not sure". The system offers three example obstacles to choose from or mix. |
| **Alternative flow A2 (skip):** The student skips the questions. The system stores the default category "unclear where to start" and continues. |
| **Acceptance Criteria** **Precondition:** •	A task exists (US004). **Postcondition:** •	The task has an obstacle category the student has confirmed or skipped. **Other conditions:** •	At most three questions are asked, and each can be answered in one tap. |
| **Exception flow:** E1: AI service unavailable. The system shows a fixed list of obstacle options instead, so the flow can continue. |

#### **2.4.6 US006: Generate Checklist** {#2.4.6-us006:-generate-checklist}

***Table 2.4.6: User Story Description for Generate Checklist***

| User story: Generate Checklist |
| ----- |
| **ID**: US006 |
| **User Story Description** **As a** student **I want** a checklist of small steps for my task **So that** I know what to do next, and for a big project I only want to see the very first step for this week |
| **Flow of events:** 1\.	The system generates a checklist from the task description, the obstacle category and the task type. For a General task it has 3 to 5 steps. The first step is marked as the Starter Step and takes about 5 minutes. 2\.	The system shows the checklist as a draft. 3\.	The student reviews it and continues to editing (US007). |
| **Alternative flow A1 (Exam Prep):** For an Exam Prep task, the checklist steps come from the accepted revision schedule (US015). |
| **Alternative flow A2 (Major Project):** For a Major Project, the system groups the steps into Phase 1, Phase 2 and so on in time order. The words "milestone" and other project-management terms are not used. After the checklist is accepted, the checklist screen shows only the first unfinished step of the current phase as "your first small step this week" and says how many steps are hidden. The student can select Show all phases to see everything. |
| **Acceptance Criteria** **Precondition:** •	The obstacle step (US005) is complete. **Postcondition:** •	A draft checklist is linked to the task and every step is marked not done. **Other conditions:** •	The checklist has at least one step and the Starter Step comes first. •	A General checklist has 3 to 5 steps. A Major Project checklist keeps its steps in phase order. •	Hidden steps are not deleted. Progress counts all steps, shown or hidden. |
| **Exception flow:** E1: AI service unavailable. The system shows an empty checklist so the student can add steps by hand (US007). |

#### **2.4.10 US010: Break Down Task Steps** {#2.4.10-us010:-break-down-task-steps}

***Table 2.4.10: User Story Description for Break Down Task Steps***

| User story: Break Down Task Steps |
| ----- |
| **ID**: US010 |
| **User Story Description** **As a** student **I want** to press Stuck on a step and have it split into smaller steps **So that** the next action feels easy to start |
| **Flow of events:** 1\.	The student selects the hint button on a checklist step. The same button is on the floating focus bar (US012). 2\.	The system shows the message "It's totally normal to feel stuck. Click here and AI will break it down even further for you." and proposes two to five smaller sub-steps. The first sub-step is a 2-minute starter action. 3\.	The student edits, adds or deletes sub-steps and selects Accept. 4\.	The system replaces the step with the sub-steps in the same position and updates the progress. |
| **Alternative flow A1 (cancel):** The student selects Cancel. The system keeps the original step. |
| **Alternative flow A2 (from the floating bar):** When the student came from the floating bar, the session continues on the first new sub-step. |
| **Acceptance Criteria** **Precondition:** •	The step is not yet done. **Postcondition:** •	The checklist is saved with the new sub-steps, all marked not done. **Other conditions:** •	Progress is recalculated from the new total number of steps. •	The wording is encouraging and never suggests the student has done something wrong. |
| **Exception flow:** E1: AI service unavailable. The system lets the student type the sub-steps by hand. E2: The student accepts with no sub-steps. The system asks for at least one. |

#### **2.4.11 US011: Start Focus Session** {#2.4.11-us011:-start-focus-session}

***Table 2.4.11: User Story Description for Start Focus Session***

| User story: Start Focus Session |
| ----- |
| **ID**: US011 |
| **User Story Description** **As a** student **I want** to open a Focus Session on one step and pick a length, including a 2-minute starter, **So that** I can begin even when I really do not want to |
| **Flow of events:** 1\.	The student selects an unfinished step and chooses Start Focus Session. 2\.	The system shows the length options: 2-minute Starter, 15 minutes, 25 minutes and 40 minutes. The student chooses one. 3\.	The student confirms. 4\.	The system creates a session record with the start time and the step, starts a soft timer and collapses the app into the floating focus bar (US012). |
| **Alternative flow A1 (timer ends):** When the timer reaches zero, the system offers Add 5 minutes or Wrap up. A student who finishes a 2-minute starter can simply keep going. |
| **Alternative flow A2 (stop early):** The student ends the session before the timer ends. The system ends the session and goes to the wrap-up (US013). |
| **Acceptance Criteria** **Precondition:** •	The task has at least one unfinished step. **Postcondition:** •	One active session exists for the chosen step. **Other conditions:** •	Only one session can be active at a time. •	The 2-minute Starter is listed before the 15, 25 and 40 minute options. •	The timer is soft: reaching zero prompts the student, but nothing is lost if they extend or stop. |
| **Exception flow:** E1: Every step is already done. The system shows a message and does not start a session. E2: The app is closed during a session. When it reopens, the system restores the session and the floating bar from its saved start time. |

#### **2.4.12 US012: Floating Focus Bar** {#2.4.12-us012:-floating-focus-bar}

***Table 2.4.12: User Story Description for Floating Focus Bar***

| User story: Floating Focus Bar |
| ----- |
| **ID**: US012 |
| **User Story Description** **As a** student **I want** a small bar in the corner that shows my timer and current step, with Stuck and Distracted buttons, **So that** I can keep reading my materials and still get help without leaving my work |
| **Flow of events:** 1\.	When a Focus Session starts, the main screen collapses into a floating bar in the bottom-right corner. 2\.	The bar shows a mini countdown, the current step, and two buttons: 💡 Stuck and 🍃 Distracted. The Stuck button carries the line "It's totally normal to feel stuck. Click here and AI will break it down even further for you." 3\.	The student works. The bar is small and does not cover reading material. 4\.	The student can pause, end early or mark the current step done from the bar. The session then goes to the wrap-up (US013). |
| **Alternative flow A1 (Stuck):** The student selects Stuck. The system saves the event and opens Break down (US010). The student accepts or edits the sub-steps, the checklist is updated and the session continues on the first new sub-step. |
| **Alternative flow A2 (Distracted):** The student selects Distracted. The system saves the event, shows a short friendly message and a Back to focus button. The student returns to the session or takes a break. |
| **Alternative flow A3 (pop out):** The student selects Pop out. The system shows the same bar in a separate mini window. Selecting Dock to app returns it to the corner. |
| **Alternative flow A4 (timer ends):** The timer reaches zero. The system offers Add 5 minutes or Wrap up. |
| **Acceptance Criteria** **Precondition:** •	A session is active (US011). **Postcondition:** •	Every Stuck and Distracted press is saved with a timestamp. **Other conditions:** •	A Distracted press never reduces XP or ends the session. •	The bar always shows the countdown, the current step, Stuck and Distracted. •	The bar and the mini window show the same session and stay in step with each other. •	This story replaces the earlier Self Check-in. The app no longer interrupts the student with periodic questions. |
| **Exception flow:** E1: AI service unavailable when Stuck is chosen. The system offers to split the step by hand instead. E2: The browser does not allow a mini window. The bar stays docked and the system explains why. |

#### **2.4.13 US013: Complete Session Wrap-up** {#2.4.13-us013:-complete-session-wrap-up}

***Table 2.4.13: User Story Description for Complete Session Wrap-up***

| User story: Complete Session Wrap-up |
| ----- |
| **ID**: US013 |
| **User Story Description** **As a** student **I want** to say what I actually did and see a fruit grow on my tree **So that** I feel progress after every session |
| **Flow of events:** 1\.	The session ends because the timer finished, the student marked the step done, or the student ended it early. 2\.	The system asks "What did you do?" with an optional note, and asks whether the step is done, partly done or parked. 3\.	The student answers. 4\.	The system updates the step status, adds XP by a fixed rule, and adds one fruit to the subject tree. The fruit shows the student's note and the session length. 5\.	The system shows the session summary. The header reads "Your trees grow with your effort. No wilted leaves, no broken streaks." A fruit drops and fades onto the tree. |
| **Alternative flow A1 (no note):** The student leaves the note empty. The system adds the fruit with the session length only. |
| **Alternative flow A2 (new achievement):** The session unlocks an achievement. The system shows it in the summary (US014). |
| **Acceptance Criteria** **Precondition:** •	A session has ended. **Postcondition:** •	The session is saved, the step status is updated, XP is increased and one fruit is added. **Other conditions:** •	XP amounts are fixed and the same for every student. •	A session stopped early still counts and still adds a fruit. XP is never removed. •	The fruit animation is short and light. When the device asks for reduced motion, the fruit appears without animation. |
| **Exception flow:** E1: Saving fails. The system keeps the wrap-up data on screen and retries when the student confirms again. |

#### **2.4.15 US015: Generate Exam Revision Schedule** {#2.4.15-us015:-generate-exam-revision-schedule}

***Table 2.4.15: User Story Description for Generate Exam Revision Schedule***

| User story: Generate Exam Revision Schedule |
| ----- |
| **ID**: US015 |
| **User Story Description** **As a** student preparing for exams **I want** my exam dates loaded for me and a revision schedule worked backward from each date **So that** I know what to study each day without typing in my timetable |
| **Flow of events:** 1\.	During onboarding or in settings, the student selects their UTM Faculty of Computing (FC) programme and semester. 2\.	The system loads the preloaded Midterm and Final exam timetable for that programme and semester, with course code (for example SECJ3563, SCSE1203), date, time and exam hall. 3\.	The system shows the exam countdown for each exam. No typing is needed. 4\.	For each exam, the system builds a revision schedule worked backward from the exam date. It spreads the course topics across the days left in phases, ending before the exam date. 5\.	The student edits the schedule and accepts it. 6\.	The system saves the schedule and creates checklist steps for each scheduled topic. |
| **Alternative flow A1 (few days left):** There are fewer days than topics. The system places several topics on the same day and tells the student that the schedule is tight. |
| **Alternative flow A2 (add quiz or test):** The student adds a quiz, test or in-class assessment that is not in the timetable, by entering the course, a name and a date. The system saves it as the student's own entry and builds its schedule in the same way. |
| **Alternative flow A3 (no timetable found):** No timetable exists for the chosen programme and semester. The system says so and the student adds exams by hand (A2). |
| **Alternative flow A4 (exam day passed):** The exam date has passed. The system shows "Exam finished" and moves the exam out of the active list without deleting it. |
| **Acceptance Criteria** **Precondition:** •	The student has chosen a programme and semester, or has added an exam by hand. **Postcondition:** •	The schedule and the matching checklist steps are saved. **Other conditions:** •	Days left equals the exam date minus today. •	Every topic appears at least once, and no scheduled date is after the exam date. •	Preloaded timetable entries are read-only. The student's own entries can be edited or deleted. •	The timetable shows when it was last updated and reminds the student to check the official notice, because dates can change. •	Homework and other General tasks are not affected. |
| **Exception flow:** E1: No topics available. The system asks the student to enter at least one topic. E2: AI service unavailable. The schedule is still built by the system's own rule, and checklist steps are created from the topic names. E3: The timetable cannot be loaded. The system shows an error and the student can add exams by hand (A2). |

## **2.5	Performance and Other Requirements** {#2.5-performance-and-other-requirements}

This section describes the non-functional requirements of StartSmart AI, including its performance, usability, reliability, security, compatibility, and maintainability.

#### **2.5.1 Performance Requirements** {#2.5.1-performance-requirements}

* **Response Time:** The system shall load the main dashboard, subject list, task details, and saved checklists within 3 seconds under normal network conditions.  
* **AI Response Time:** The system should generate AI-assisted responses, including task obstacle guidance, checklist generation, hints, and task breakdowns, within 10 seconds under normal conditions. If the response takes longer or the AI service is unavailable, the system shall display an appropriate message and provide an alternative where possible.  
* **Data Processing:** The system shall save and update task details, checklist progress, session records, and experience points within 3 seconds under normal conditions.

#### **2.5.2 Software System Attributes** {#2.5.2-software-system-attributes}

* **Usability:** The system shall provide a simple and intuitive user interface that allows students to create tasks, manage checklists, and track their progress with minimal difficulty. Instructions and error messages shall use clear and understandable language.  
* **Reliability:** The system shall save user data accurately and maintain task and checklist progress across sessions. If the AI service is unavailable, the system shall provide alternative options, such as predefined obstacle choices or manual checklist creation, where applicable.  
* **Security:** The system shall require user authentication before allowing access to personal academic tasks and saved progress. Passwords shall be stored securely, and communication between the browser and server shall be protected using HTTPS in deployment.  
* **Privacy:** The system shall only collect information necessary for its intended functions. Students' task descriptions, saved conversations, and academic progress shall not be accessible to other unauthorized users.  
* **Maintainability:** The system shall be developed using a modular structure so that components such as task management, AI assistance, checklist management, and progress tracking can be maintained and updated independently where practical.  
* **Accessibility:** The system shall use readable text, clear labels, consistent navigation, and sufficient colour contrast to improve accessibility for students with different needs.  
* **Recoverability:** The system shall display appropriate error messages when saving or loading data fails. Where possible, it shall allow students to retry the operation without having to re-enter previously submitted information.

# **2.6	Design Constraints** {#2.6-design-constraints}

The following constraints define the limitations and conditions that must be considered when designing and implementing StartSmart AI. 

#### **2.6.1 Platform Constraints** {#2.6.1-platform-constraints}

* **Web Application:** StartSmart AI shall be developed as a web application accessible through a web browser. The initial implementation shall not require users to install a separate desktop or mobile application.  
* **Internet Connectivity:** An internet connection shall be required to access the web application, communicate with the server, save data remotely, and use online AI services.  
* **Browser Compatibility:** The system shall use web technologies supported by the targeted modern browsers. Browser-specific features that prevent consistent operation across supported browsers should be avoided.

#### **2.6.2 Technical Constraints** {#2.6.2-technical-constraints}

* **AI Service Dependency:** AI-assisted features shall depend on the availability of the selected AI service. The system shall provide predefined or manual alternatives for supported functions when the AI service is unavailable. AI service credentials shall be stored securely on the server and shall not be exposed in client-side code.  
* **Data Storage:** User accounts, subjects, tasks, checklists, saved conversations, and progress records shall be stored in a suitable database. Access to stored information shall be controlled to prevent unauthorized access.  
* **Responsive Interface:** The user interface shall be designed to accommodate desktop, tablet, and mobile screen sizes without requiring a separate application for each device.

#### **2.6.3 Security and Privacy Constraints** {#2.6.3-security-and-privacy-constraints}

* **Authentication and Access Control:** The system shall implement authentication and access control to ensure that students can access only the academic information they are authorized to view or modify.  
* **Data Protection:** Sensitive information shall be transmitted securely, and passwords shall be stored using an appropriate password-hashing mechanism. Personal information sent to the AI service shall be limited to what is necessary for the requested function.

#### **2.6.4 Project Constraints** {#2.6.4-project-constraints}

* **Development Time:** The system shall be designed and implemented within the allocated academic project period. Therefore, development shall prioritize the essential features, including account management, subject and task management, AI-assisted checklist generation, checklist progress tracking, and saved task history.  
* **Project Scope:** Advanced features such as camera-based or screen-based AI monitoring, real-time peer collaboration, past-year examination paper analysis, and heatmap calendars shall be excluded from the initial implementation. These features may be considered for future development.  
* **Student-Controlled Workflow:** The system shall allow students to edit AI-generated checklists and manage their own task progress. AI-generated suggestions shall support students' decisions rather than prevent them from organizing their work according to their needs.
